Perceptual statistics for every Glyos palette

Source: R/usecase.R
glyos_palette_stats.Rd

Computes, from the hex colors alone, how suitable each palette is for the common plotting jobs. Used by glyos_find_palettes(); exposed so you can apply your own thresholds.

Usage

glyos_palette_stats(names = glyos_palette_names())

Arguments

names

Palette names to compute for. Defaults to all palettes.

Value

A data frame with one row per palette and the columns:

palette

Palette name.

n_colours

Number of colors.

min_de

Smallest pairwise Lab distance between any two colors. Larger is easier to tell apart; 20 is a comfortable floor for categorical use.

min_de_deutan, min_de_protan, min_de_tritan

The same after simulating each color-vision deficiency.

lum_range

Range of CIE lightness (0 to 100) across the palette.

hue_spread

Angular spread of the chromatic colors' hues, in degrees. Near 0 means one hue family.

hue_clusters

Number of distinct hue families (hues separated by more than 60 degrees).

has_light

Whether the palette contains a light or neutral color that can serve as a midpoint.

categorical, colorblind, sequential, diverging

Logical flags as used by glyos_find_palettes().

Details

Distances are CIE76 (Euclidean in CIE Lab). Color-vision deficiency is simulated with the Machado, Oliveira and Fernandes (2009) matrices at full severity for deuteranopia, protanopia and tritanopia. Hue statistics only consider colors with chroma of at least 20, so grays and blacks do not count as a hue.

Examples

s <- glyos_palette_stats()
head(s[order(-s$min_de_deutan), c("palette", "min_de", "min_de_deutan")])
#>                  palette   min_de min_de_deutan
#> 88       osm_alpha_phase 68.70507      49.76224
#> 78           rf_sentinel 47.62056      48.83391
#> 69 bt_livid_dracosaurian 38.22175      37.96039
#> 76          rf_maxx_zero 40.68568      34.57933
#> 91     osm_jack_asteroid 38.14048      32.93691
#> 92           osm_mystron 33.17829      29.66489
